name: Board Meeting Presentation Deck
description: A six-page, decision-first board pre-read and live-meeting deck in warm white, midnight navy, and restrained orange for surfacing quarterly performance, material strategic bets, explicit risks, formal resolutions, accountable owners, and the next 90 days of execution.
style_guide:
# Decision-First Board Meeting Presentation Deck

## Design intent

Create a board working document that helps directors understand what changed, test management's interpretation, debate material tradeoffs, cast clearly worded votes, and leave with named owners and dated follow-through. This is not a ceremonial company overview and not a dense archive of everything management knows. Every page should earn its place by supporting a board duty: oversight, approval, challenge, risk review, capital allocation, succession, or accountability.

The visual system alternates warm-white analytical pages with midnight-navy decision moments. Restrained burnt orange marks agenda logic, vote identifiers, thresholds, deadlines, and the one point that requires attention. Red, amber, and green may appear only as explicit status semantics; they are not members of the primary palette.

The preview images define composition, pacing, hierarchy, and visual character only. They are not a source of truth. Do not reuse any preview company, security symbol, presenter, director, date, quarter, metric, financial result, resolution, transaction, risk, owner, source, recommendation, or conclusion. Rebuild all content from the current workspace and identify any remaining assumption or placeholder.

## Core visual signature

- Use an editorial governance aesthetic: large sentence-case conclusions, quiet evidence fields, strict rules, narrow metadata, and disciplined whitespace.
- Open with a split dark-light context page or a dark cover that immediately identifies meeting type, period, document status, presenter, quorum context, agenda, reading budget, and number of decisions.
- Keep most evidence pages warm white so tables and financial comparisons remain legible; reserve full navy pages for the cover, formal decisions, meeting close, or an exceptional section reset.
- Use orange as a directional thread rather than decoration: agenda step, decision ID, attention rail, voting action, target line, due date, or active milestone.
- Prefer one board question per page and write the answer as the page title. Avoid generic titles such as “Financial Update” when the evidence supports a precise conclusion.
- Pair every adverse variance, open risk, and requested decision with a named owner, next action, date, and consequence.

## Canvas, grid, and spacing

- Author on a fixed 16:9 canvas at 1920 × 1080 or an equivalent aspect ratio.
- Keep essential content inside 80–96 px side margins and 48–72 px top and bottom margins. Edge rails, background fields, and footer bands may bleed.
- Use a 12-column grid with 20–28 px gutters. Tables, scorecards, resolution ledgers, risk rows, and roadmap milestones must share the same column anchors.
- Reserve 150–220 px for the eyebrow, page conclusion, explanatory subhead, and any compact quorum or timer panel.
- Use 28–40 px between major zones, 16–24 px between related cards, and 8–12 px within label-value groups.
- Prefer square cards or corners no larger than 6 px. Use hairline borders and almost no shadow.
- Keep body copy at 17–22 px, table text at 14–18 px, source notes at 12–15 px, and critical values at 30–52 px. If content does not fit, shorten, split, or move detail to an appendix.

## Color system

### Primary palette

- Warm white: #F6F3ED. Default analytical canvas, table field, evidence card, and document surface.
- Midnight navy: #11192C. Cover field, decision-close page, primary text, quorum panel, and high-contrast container.
- Burnt orange: #C75B08. Agenda markers, vote IDs, required actions, target lines, due dates, and selected milestones.
- Ink black: #10131A. Strong table rules and text on light backgrounds.
- Quiet slate: #7D8BA5. Metadata, secondary labels, chart context, and non-material comparison.
- Pale rule: #DDD9D1. Row separators, neutral borders, and table scaffolding.

### Semantic exceptions

- Governance green: #12B886 only for on-track, approved, completed, or threshold-met states.
- Review amber: #F59F00 only for watch, review, near-threshold, or unresolved but contained states.
- Material red: #F04444 only for off-plan, high/open, breached, rejected, or time-critical states.
- Status colors must always be paired with text such as On track, Watch, High · Open, Approve, or Breached.
- These exception colors do not belong in the preset's three primary color tags and must never become decorative page accents.

## Typography

- Use Inter, Arial, Aptos, or another neutral grotesk sans serif for page conclusions, tables, scorecards, resolution language, risk text, and owner details.
- Use Source Serif 4, Georgia, or another restrained editorial serif only when a short quotation, closing line, or formal framing benefits from institutional gravity.
- Use IBM Plex Mono, Roboto Mono, or an equivalent mono face for page numbers, agenda IDs, resolution IDs, periods, thresholds, dates, vote states, sources, and confidentiality.
- Use italic sans or serif sparingly for one explanatory sentence beneath the title. Italic text should clarify the operating rule, not carry dense evidence.
- Cover titles may be 60–94 px; analytical conclusions 42–62 px; card titles 21–28 px; table body 14–18 px.
- Prefer sentence case. All caps are limited to short eyebrows, table labels, classification, and compact operational metadata.
- Keep currency, units, sign, reporting basis, period, and comparison reference visually attached to every number.

## Persistent frame

- Place a short chapter eyebrow at upper left and a two-digit page counter at upper right.
- Carry meeting period, document status, evidence cutoff, and confidentiality in a quiet footer where applicable.
- On live-meeting pages, show time allocation or vote count in a compact high-contrast panel.
- Use a stable language system: fact, management view, board question, recommendation, resolution, owner, due date, consequence, status, source.
- Resolution identifiers must persist from executive summary through vote ledger and next-step roadmap.
- Risk identifiers, initiative numbers, and KPI labels must not change between summary and detail pages.

## Page archetypes

### Cover, meeting context, and agenda

Identify the legal entity or organization, meeting type, reporting period, document status, presenter, co-presenter, preparation date, meeting date, location or channel, quorum status, reading budget, and confidentiality. List the small number of slides and mark which ones inform, invite discussion, require a vote, or close an action. If quorum or notice has not been verified, label it pending rather than implying compliance.

### Executive summary and resolutions

Lead with two to four quarter-level conclusions: momentum, variance, external change, or matter requiring board action. Below them, present each proposed resolution verbatim or clearly mark draft language. Include proposer, committee review, management recommendation, financial or governance effect, approval threshold, and exact action requested. Keep management's recommendation distinct from the Board's decision.

### CEO scorecard and core metrics

Show only the metrics directors need to evaluate strategy and stewardship. Use plan, actual, variance, status, remediation, owner, and date in consistent columns. Green rows need little commentary; every amber or red row needs a specific explanation and corrective action. Define GAAP or non-GAAP basis, currency, cohort, time period, and source. Use compact supporting charts only where trend or mix adds insight.

### Strategic initiative progress

Limit the page to three or four material bets. For each, state strategic promise, measurable milestone, current evidence, trajectory, owner, next gate, board ask, and downside if delayed. Use one chart or progress structure per bet. Never substitute activity counts for strategic outcomes.

### Material risks and mitigations

Use plain English: risk event, exposure, specific consequence, likelihood or status, control or mitigation, accountable owner, next action, completion date, and escalation trigger. Align legal or public-company risks with the appropriate disclosure taxonomy only when verified. A decorative empty heat map is not a risk assessment; use a matrix only when likelihood and impact definitions are explicit.

### Board decisions and next steps

Restate the exact resolutions, voting action, owner, immediate execution task, first check-back, and route from committee to full board. Pair the vote ledger with a 30-, 60-, or 90-day roadmap. End with the next meeting or review date and what written evidence will return to the Board. Do not mark a decision approved until the recorded vote supports that state.

## Six-page narrative contract

- Treat the six preview archetypes as a strong default route: meeting context, executive decisions, performance scorecard, strategic bets, material risks, and recorded decisions with next steps.
- The executive-summary page establishes identifiers for every proposed resolution. Reuse those exact identifiers on the close and in any follow-up roadmap.
- The scorecard supplies the performance evidence behind discussion; the initiative page shows how management is responding; the risk page exposes what may still prevent delivery.
- The final page must reconcile every requested vote, owner, check-back date, and 90-day milestone. Nothing introduced as a decision on page two should disappear at the close.
- Adapt the sequence only when board duties or meeting purpose require it. Preserve the decision-to-evidence-to-accountability logic even when page count changes.

## Data and governance integrity

- Preview facts are visual placeholders only. Never copy preview names, companies, symbols, dates, metrics, board composition, results, transactions, policies, risks, owners, or votes.
- Distinguish observed fact, management statement, external source, estimate, forecast, target, scenario, legal advice, committee recommendation, and board action.
- Reconcile financial values to the current approved reporting package. Preserve currency, scale, period, accounting basis, consolidation scope, comparison baseline, and rounding.
- Never invent revenue, margin, cash flow, leverage, dilution, headcount, retention, pipeline, transaction price, legal exposure, quorum, vote, or approval.
- If a value is unavailable, show pending, not provided, to be confirmed, or an explicit question. Do not fill gaps with plausible numbers.
- Define RAG thresholds before assigning colors. A red variance must not become green on another page without a dated status change.
- Every forecast or target requires an as-of date, horizon, owner, and key assumption. Separate base plan from upside and downside scenarios.
- Every resolution must have exact language, authority, approval threshold, conflicts process where relevant, and recorded result. Do not paraphrase legal text into a different obligation.
- Keep privileged, confidential, personal, market-sensitive, and insider information appropriately classified. Do not infer that distribution is permitted because a preview looks polished.
- Claims about law, regulation, listing rules, accounting treatment, governance standards, committee clearance, or disclosure obligations require current authoritative verification.
- Include source or methodology notes next to material charts and tables. A footer saying “internal data” is insufficient when multiple systems or cutoffs differ.
- Show dissent, uncertainty, and alternative interpretations where material. A board deck should make challenge possible, not manufacture unanimity.
- Avoid false precision. Round estimates appropriately and state sensitivity where a small assumption changes the conclusion.

## Charts, tables, and diagrams

- Prefer variance tables, contribution bridges, small trend charts, milestone plots, risk ledgers, decision registers, and dated roadmaps.
- Begin axes at zero when magnitude comparison requires it; otherwise disclose truncation. Label units directly and avoid dual axes unless indispensable.
- Use orange target lines and direct data labels. Keep legends close to the marks they explain.
- Use a maximum of seven scorecard rows, four resolutions, four material risks, or three strategic bets on one ordinary page.
- Keep table rules light but make column meaning explicit. Do not rely on alignment alone to distinguish plan, actual, and variance.
- Use icons only for explicit states such as vote, risk, owner, date, source, or decision. Avoid ornamental corporate iconography.
- Photographs are usually unnecessary. If used, restrict them to the cover or a verified operational context and never use a stock image as evidence.

## Content and facilitation rules

- Every page should answer: What happened? Why does it matter to the Board? What must directors discuss, decide, or monitor?
- Put the management conclusion in the title and expose the evidence beneath it.
- Separate pre-read detail from meeting-time content. The meeting should focus on exceptions, tradeoffs, and decisions rather than reading tables aloud.
- Phrase board asks as actions: approve, authorize, adopt, ratify, discuss, note, or direct. Avoid vague asks such as “support” or “align.”
- Pair every owner with a role, due date, deliverable, and escalation path.
- Keep appendix material available for definitions, reconciliations, committee history, scenario detail, and source extracts without crowding the main six-page narrative.

## Allowed variation

- The deck may support public, private, nonprofit, family-owned, or regulated boards, but governance terms and decision authority must match the actual entity.
- A full-dark page may be used for cover, formal vote, crisis decision, or close. Most evidence pages remain warm white.
- The number of resolutions, risks, KPIs, and strategic bets may change, provided the page remains readable and materiality is explicit.
- Orange may appear as a left rail, top rule, numeral, target line, or action button. It must not flood large analytical surfaces.
- The agenda may be organized by fiduciary duty, decision type, strategic theme, or meeting sequence.

## Avoid

- Do not reuse preview organizations, people, financials, transactions, dates, risks, policies, resolutions, owners, or sources.
- Do not bury a material miss inside averages, decorative dashboards, or an appendix.
- Do not present management recommendation as board approval.
- Do not claim quorum, committee clearance, legal compliance, audit review, or shareholder authorization without evidence.
- Do not show confidential live data in a broadly distributed visual without correct classification.
- Do not use tiny text, dense spreadsheet screenshots, unexplained acronyms, 3D charts, gradients, glass effects, or stock boardroom photography.
- Do not assign color without a written state or threshold.
- Do not leave a risk, resolution, or strategic initiative without owner and date.
- Do not end with “Questions.” End with the decisions taken, actions assigned, and evidence that will return.
